body:
> Extracted 2026-09-01 while decomposing #223 (the tool posture) and #217 (the capability map). Both change how
> a worker's permitted tools are *derived*, and #217's own body flags the collision: "if both land, the grant
> should be derived from the union of the map and the posture rather than maintained twice."

## Why

Today "what may this worker use" is answered by reading `profile.allowed_tools` at the launch site and nowhere
else. That was fine while it was one hand-maintained list. It is about to stop being one:

- **#223** wants the answer to depend on a posture (`inherit` vs `curate`) and on MCP servers named or excluded.
- **#217** wants part of the answer *derived* — if a profile binds an intent to something invoked with `Skill`,
  then `Skill` is granted because of that binding rather than because somebody remembered to type it.
- **#223** also wants a card to be able to **narrow** the profile's grant, and never to widen it.

Three sources, one output, and no single place that combines them. Land either feature first and it reaches into
the launch directly; land the second and it either overwrites the first's reasoning or bolts a second derivation
beside it. That is exactly the drift that produced #114 — a field naming a capability and a launch granting it,
maintained separately, disagreeing silently under `dontAsk` where an unlisted tool is denied rather than
prompted.

This card builds **only the seam**. No posture, no map, no new configuration, no behaviour change: today's
inputs through today's rules, with one function that both siblings can plug into instead of into `src/board.js`.

## What

- **`effectiveTools(profile, task, board)` in `src/model.js`** — pure, no I/O — returning the tool list a launch
  should use, plus what it dropped and why. Today that is `profile.allowed_tools` unchanged; the value is the
  shape, not the logic.
- **A card narrows, never widens.** `kb.tools` / `kb.mcp` on a task intersect with the profile's grant. Anything
  a card asks for that its profile does not have is **dropped and recorded**, never granted — a card that could
  widen its own permissions is the seat problem one rung down. The dropped list is returned, not swallowed, so a
  caller can say so.
- **Extension points, unused here**: the signature takes what the two siblings will need (the profile, the card,
  the board) so neither has to change it. Do not implement a posture or a map — a stub for either is worse than
  a clean seam, because it invites a second one.
- **The launch site calls it.** `src/board.js` / `src/dispatch.js` stop reading `allowed_tools` directly and ask
  `effectiveTools` instead. That is the whole point: after this, there is exactly one answer to the question.
- **Tests are the deliverable as much as the function**: today's behaviour is byte-identical for every existing
  profile — a test asserts the launch line is unchanged for the shipped `claude`, `claude-track` and `claude-p`
  — and the narrowing rule is pinned, including the widening attempt that gets dropped and reported.

## Done when

- [ ] `effectiveTools(profile, task, board)` is exported from `src/model.js`, pure, and returns both the list and
      what it dropped.
- [ ] Every existing profile produces a byte-identical launch line to today's, pinned by a test.
- [ ] A card narrowing its profile's grant works; a card attempting to widen it is dropped and reported, with a
      test for each.
- [ ] Nothing outside `effectiveTools` reads `profile.allowed_tools` to build a launch.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass. No new configuration key ships in this card.
goal: effectiveTools(profile, task, board) is the single pure derivation of a launch's tool list, returning what it dropped; a card can narrow but never widen; every shipped profile's launch line is byte-identical to today's, pinned by a test; nothing else reads allowed_tools to build a launch
title: One place derives what a worker may use, so the posture and the capability map do not each grow their own answer
